channel.title: Delta Owl Eyes — News Updates
channel.description: Verified updates on Canada's Truth and Reconciliation Commission Calls to Action.

item.title: Indigenous child-welfare authority and northern medical transportation raise accountability questions
item.description: Yellowknives Dene child welfare: Reporting published October 29 says Northwest Territories Premier R.J. Simpson committed to beginning discussions with Yellowknives Dene First Nations about formalizing their child and family services authority. Community representatives raised concerns about children separated from siblings, limited local services and disconnection from culture. The commitment to discuss authority is not a finalized agreement or evidence that services have changed.

item.title: Kuujjuaq secures $1 million federal contribution for local food production
item.description: Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions announced a $1 million non-repayable contribution to the Northern Village of Kuujjuaq on October 30, 2026. The community-led greenhouse project is intended to expand local food production through a new building connected to an existing greenhouse, equipment for food preservation, and space for harvest processing and fresh-food growing workshops.

item.title: Canada announces additional $130 million for Inuit-led housing
item.description: On October 30, Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada announced an additional $130 million for Inuit Treaty Organizations through the Urban, Rural and Northern Indigenous Housing Strategy. The government says this brings the allocation to approximately $327.8 million. Funding can support new housing, repairs, transitional housing, rent subsidies and other Inuit-led priorities. Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami President Natan Obed welcomed direct investment in rights-holding organizations.

item.title: Mi’kmawey Debert Cultural Centre receives $1.042 million commitment for educational trails
item.description: On October 29, 2026, the governments of Canada and Nova Scotia announced funding for three accessible educational trails at the Mi’kmawey Debert Cultural Centre in Debert, Nova Scotia. The federal contribution is $942,000 through the Active Transportation Fund, with $100,000 from the province. The announcement coincided with an event marking the start of construction on the cultural centre.

item.title: Manitoba gives Indigenous Heritage Month legislation royal assent
item.description: On October 29, 2026, the Legislative Assembly of Manitoba recorded royal assent for Bill 231, the Indigenous Heritage Month Act. The legislation amends the province's Commemoration of Days, Weeks and Months Act to recognize September each year as Indigenous Heritage Month. MLA Billie Cross introduced the bill, describing it as an opportunity to recognize First Nations, Métis and Inuit cultures, histories and contributions.

item.title: Northern Manitoba training initiative receives $250,000 for surveyor careers
item.description: On October 28, 2026, Prairies Economic Development Canada announced $250,000 for the Northern Manitoba Sector Council to develop and deliver a Surveyor Assistant training program. University College of the North's Northern Manitoba Mining Academy in Flin Flon is to provide technical learning, followed by work-integrated experience with mining and industry partners. The announcement says placements have been secured with Alamos Gold, Vale, Hudbay Minerals and Manitoba's Highways department.

item.title: First Nations and First Ministers discuss infrastructure, safety and a proposed sovereign wealth fund
item.description: On October 26, Prime Minister Mark Carney convened First Nations leaders and provincial and territorial premiers to discuss economic participation, infrastructure and community safety. The federal government announced $260 million over four years for Indigenous workforce readiness, more than $2.5 billion over five years for emergency management and fire protection measures, and more than $630 million over four years to renew and expand First Nations and Inuit policing agreements, alongside proposed ongoing funding. Leaders also discussed potential revenue-sharing arrangements and a First Nations Sovereign Wealth Fund; no established fund was announced.

item.title: New Cree Nations Miyoyawin Centre completed: relevant context for Call to Action 21
item.description: Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation and Indigenous Services Canada announced completion of a culturally supportive residential treatment and healing centre in Saskatchewan. The federal government reported a $29.3 million project investment and the First Nation a further $1.8 million for detoxification space that is not yet operational. This is relevant context for Indigenous-led healing, but the announcement does not establish that TRC Call to Action 21 has been fulfilled or that ongoing operating funding is secured.
